links.outcome: Snake species classification accuracy on validation set versus real-world external test images
links.effect: Accuracy fell from 95.6% (validation) to 83.3% (external test, no preprocessing); TT-ODC preprocessing raised it to 89.8% versus 90.3% for human annotation.
links.quote: Without preprocessing, the model achieved 95.6% accuracy on the validation set but dropped to 83.3% on the external test set.

links.outcome: Overestimation of accuracy on internal validation data versus external test data
links.effect: Validation accuracy of 95.6% overstated real-world performance; the external test set gave 83.3% accuracy without preprocessing.
links.quote: Without preprocessing, the model achieved 95.6% accuracy on the validation set but dropped to 83.3% on the external test set.

unlisted_practices: Test-time object detection and cropping (TT-ODC) preprocessing to close the gap between validation and real-world image performance

screen.reason: The study evaluates the deployment of an image classification tool via a chatbot and specifically tests an automated preprocessing safeguard/practice (test-time object detection and cropping) to improve real-world input accuracy on external user-submitted images.

primary.practice: test-time object detection and cropping preprocessing
